_sources_note: Compiled 2026-11-03 ~2pm ET from web search. Margins are D minus R in points for the statewide top race (2024 = President except OH = U.S. Senate; 2022 = Gov/Senate as noted). 2024 vote-type margins come from NBC News/NEP 'votes by type' tables (within-type candidate % rounded to whole points, so each margin is +/-1pt; 'pre' is the vote-weighted combination of early+mail computed from those rounded %s). Pre shares are pre-Election-Day (early in-person + mail) fraction of total ballots; 2022 shares mostly from AP Decision Notes ('about X% cast early or absentee'). 2026 early-vote counts from local press quoting state election offices and the callthemap.com/early-vote tracker (Oct 30 - Nov 3 2026); sources disagree by a few %. null = not found, NOT estimated. turnout_factor_guess = analyst judgment (low-moderate confidence): assumes early-vote surge partly cannibalizes Election Day (early share keeps rising each cycle), so total turnout ratio << pre-vote ratio. NC (2022+2024), GA 2022 and SC 2022 margins are exact computations from official/OpenElections precinct files with vote-method columns (higher confidence than NBC-derived rows). KEY PATTERN: in the 2022 midterm the early-vs-ED partisan gap was ~20-25pt in NC/GA/SC, far larger than in 2024 (~4-10pt) - use 2022 gaps as the midterm prior, and 2026 early electorates look even more D-leaning than 2022 where party data exist (NC, FL).

KY.order_notes: AP (2026 Decision Notes): almost all counties post ALL absentee + early results in the first report, and most counties also include in-person Election Day votes in that same first report -> first dumps are largely full-county, not pre-only; treat as mixed (county-complete). Fayette Co. (Lexington, D) posts absentee first, then early+ED as precincts deliver. 2024: first results 6:05pm ET, 50% at 8:15pm ET, 90% at 9:30pm ET. Mail absentee must be RECEIVED by 6pm local on ED (no postmark grace) -> essentially nothing late except provisionals. Western KY (Central time) closes 7pm ET. Pre-ED vote is small (~23% in 2022), and only ~11% of 2026 pre-ED is mail (excused absentee). Vote-type partisan lean not found statewide (NBC does not break KY out by type). 2024 early voters were 52.6% R / 40.3% D by registration; 2026 day-1 early voters were D-plurality by registration (66,166 D vs 60,793 R) - registration is a weak proxy in KY (many registered Ds vote R) but the swing in registered-party mix of early voters vs 2024 is notable (moderate D-enthusiasm signal). Confidence: order moderate-high; margins none.

early_vote_2026.party_split: registration only: day-1 early in-person 66,166 D / 60,793 R / 8,942 other; mail 47,866 vs in-person 390,736 (callthemap). 2022 final pre-ED = 337,975 (SOS). 2024 final early+excused = 792,476 (52.6% R / 40.3% D reg).
early_vote_2026.as_of: 2026-11-02 (SOS Adams; early in-person + absentee through Oct 31)

IN.order_notes: AP (2026 Decision Notes): officials in more than three-quarters of the 92 counties are expected to include nearly all absentee and early results in their FIRST update; absentee ballots may be counted as received, before polls close. In Indiana 'absentee' = early in-person + mail. ED precincts follow. 2024: first results 6:05pm ET, 50% at 8:30pm ET, 90% at 11:49pm ET. Polls close 6pm local; NW (Lake/Porter, Gary/Chicago suburbs, D-heavy) and SW (Evansville area) corners are Central time -> 7pm ET, so Lake County arrives later and is D-leaning (late D skew from geography, not vote type). Mail must be received by close of polls on ED (no postmark grace; not re-verified for 2026). Vote-type margins: NBC 2024 broke out only 9% of IN votes by type (mail 62-36 Trump, early in-person 73-25 Trump in reporting counties) - not representative, not used. IN mail voting requires an excuse (age 65+, etc.) so mail is NOT strongly D as in other states. Record early vote in Marion (86,597 vs 49,381 in 2022, Indianapolis, D) and Hamilton (~70k vs 40k; suburban, school referendums) and St. Joseph (~30k vs 6k) -> early vote likely more D than 2022. Confidence: order moderate; margins none.

early_vote_2026.party_split: no party registration in IN. Early in-person 714,724 (Election Division prelim) to 755,000+ (Capital Chronicle) vs 538,623 in 2022 and 1,397,163 in 2024. Total absentee ~848k-885k vs ~689k in 2022.

FL.order_notes: AP: counties release all or almost all early in-person AND mail results in their first update, usually before any ED results; counties expect to post early+mail ~30 min after polls close (7pm local; Panhandle 8pm ET). ED precincts follow through the evening; ~99% reported by midnight in 2020. Mail must be RECEIVED by 7pm ED (no postmark grace; only overseas/military up to 10 days). Late: mail dropped off on ED (counted after election night in some counties), provisionals. Key correction: first dump is pre-ED votes, which in 2024 were ~R+9 vs final R+13 (ED R+25), i.e. first dump understates R by ~4pt in a presidential year; in 2026 the early electorate is much more D than 2022/2024 (D turnout rate 49% vs R 38%), so the first dump should be markedly more D than the final and ED votes should be strongly R. 2024 early in-person was strongly R (R+24) while mail was D (D+17) - the split between the two matters. Note FL 2024 shares below are of the 92% of votes NBC broke out by type.

early_vote_2026.party_split: pre-ED by registration: R 2,194,546 / D 2,065,302 / NPA+other 1,205,342 (R+2.4 of ballots). Mail: D ~832-855k vs R ~679-697k; early in-person: R ~1.50M vs D ~1.21M; NPA ~669k in person + ~382k mail. Turnout rate: D 49% vs R 38% vs NPA 31% (R have 1.5M registration edge, big unvoted R bench for ED). 5.4M = 69% of total 2022 turnout (7,796,916).

GA.order_notes: Counties may begin tabulating mail ballots at 7am ED; first election-night results include most mail + early in-person votes (AP). ED precincts follow; GA is historically slower (2020: ~77% reported by midnight). In 2022 Warnock led by ~40pt in first batches, margin fell below 1pt after ~2 hours -> first dumps are heavily D-skewed because the large metro-Atlanta counties' pre-ED votes post first. Mail must be RECEIVED by 7pm ED (UOCAVA 3-day grace). Late: provisionals, UOCAVA, plus slow ED reporting in Fulton/DeKalb/Gwinnett. 2022 Gov (Kemp): NBC shows Kemp top in early in-person and ED, Abrams top in mail (exact within-type margins not found). 2022 Senate: Warnock top in early in-person and mail, Walker top on ED. 2024: early in-person was only R+3 and ED R+7 (statewide early vs ED gap small; geography/order matters more than vote type). 2022 margins = U.S. Senate first round (Warnock D+0.9 final), computed from OpenElections GA precinct file (ED 1,410,749 / advance in-person 2,276,270 / mail 245,935 / prov 2,970; matches NBC totals). Governor 2022 (Kemp R+7.5) in the same file is missing Gwinnett: excluding Gwinnett, ED -26.7 / early -1.8 / mail +25.8 / pre +0.9 - so the Gov early-vs-ED gap was ~25pt in 2022 vs only ~4pt in 2024.

early_vote_2026.party_split: no party registration. In-person ~2.69M + absentee 118,329. SOS certified figure 2,828,147. 2022 pre-ED record ~2.5M. ED: 300k+ voted by 10am, SOS expects >1M on ED.

NC.order_notes: County boards may tabulate mail ballots before polls close; first reports (~7:30-8pm ET) are early one-stop + mail; ED precincts follow. 2022: Beasley led Budd by ~20pt in first batches, lead disappeared after ~90 minutes (Budd won by 3.2). Only ~1% of vote uncounted after election night. 2023 law (SB 747) ended the 3-day postmark grace: civilian mail must be RECEIVED by 7:30pm ED (2026 in force); only UOCAVA later. Late: provisionals, UOCAVA. Margins computed from NCSBE official precinct file (results_pct, columns Election Day / One Stop / Absentee by Mail): 2024 President ED 1,169,088 / one-stop 4,208,839 / mail 295,602 / prov 25,612; 2022 Senate (Budd R+3.2 final) ED 1,571,681 / one-stop 2,003,761 / mail 186,810 / prov 11,672. Note the early-vs-ED gap was 25pt in 2022 (midterm) vs 10pt in 2024. 2026 early electorate is much more D than 2022 by registration (D+12.3 vs D+7.0 same point 2022), mail absentee down ~35% vs 2022.

early_vote_2026.party_split: D 1,085,321 / R 738,748 / U 1,004,205 (registered-party gap D+12.3 vs D+7.0 at same point 2022). In-person 2,728,268, mail 100,020.

VA.order_notes: Polls close 7pm ET; localities begin reporting ~7:10pm. Since the 2022 law early/absentee results are reported back to precincts and many localities (e.g. Fairfax City by 7:18pm in 2025) now post early votes early in the night, but practice varies by locality: some central absentee precincts (CAPs, mail-heavy, very D) still report late at night, and historically (2020) initial in-person precinct returns favored R while early/absentee, reported late, were heavily D. Also rural ED precincts tend to report fast. Mail postmarked by ED counts if RECEIVED by noon Fri Nov 6 2026 (3-day grace) -> late mail is a real late mode, strongly D (2024 mail D+48). Localities report additional absentees Nov 4-6. HB968 (2026) changes absentee processing for the 2026 general - details not verified. No 2022 statewide race (House only) -> 2022 margins null. Confidence: order low-moderate (locality-dependent).

early_vote_2026.party_split: no party registration. In-person ~1.32M, mail returned ~328k. Fairfax +62% vs 2022 (2022: 140,225). 2022 final pre-ED 976,558 (VPAP).

SC.order_notes: AP (2026): counties vary. About half release all/almost all mail results in the first update, and about half of those also release ED results at the same time; almost every county releases at least some early in-person results in the first update. 2024 first results 7:19pm ET. Polls close 7pm ET. Mail absentee must be RECEIVED by 7pm ED (no grace). Late: provisionals. Early in-person ~R+17 and ED R+23 in 2024 -> small early/ED gap; mail (tiny, ~4%) D+13. Pre-ED share jumped from 36% (2022) to 62% (2024), so 2026 early-vote ratio vs 2022 overstates turnout growth. 2022 margins = Governor (McMaster R+17.5 final) from OpenElections SC precinct file (ED 1,084,813 / early 542,512 / mail 69,790 / prov+failsafe 6,077): early vote was nearly even in 2022 but ED R+25 -> 2022 early-vs-ED gap ~21pt vs ~6pt in 2024.

early_vote_2026.party_split: no party registration. ~1.04M early in-person (vs 561,563 in 2022) + 42,528 absentee returned (Nov 3 report). 2022 total ~1.7M.
early_vote_2026.as_of: 2026-11-02 (SC Election Commission via WIS / SC Public Radio)

OH.order_notes: AP: first votes reported after 7:30pm ET poll close are mail + early in-person ('absentee'), which have favored Ds; D leads eroded over the next ~2 hours as ED votes came in (Vance overtook Ryan ~9:30pm ET in 2022; Trump likewise in 2020). NEW FOR 2026: mail ballots must be RECEIVED by 7:30pm ED (postmark grace period eliminated; 2026 primary late-arriving ballots fell to 1,564) -> late mail mode largely gone; remaining late: provisionals, UOCAVA. 2024 margins below are for U.S. Senate (Brown-Moreno) and cover only 60% of votes broken out by type (partial, likely skewed to counties that report by type).

early_vote_2026.party_split: no party registration. Mail ~654k, in-person ~1.10M (callthemap, rounded). SOS: >1.7M vs nearly 1.5M in 2022 (record for gubernatorial year). 2022 total 4.13M.
